tasks.title: Eagles on the Caraiman Cross
tasks.statement:
The tallest cross built on a mountain peak is located on a plateau situated on the top of the peak called Caraiman in Romania at altitude H = 2300 m from the sea level. Its height, including the base-support is h = 39.3 m. The horizontal arms of the cross are oriented on the N-S direction. The latitude at which the Cross is located is φ = 45º.

A) On the evening of 21st of March 2014, the vernal equinox day, two eagles stop from their flight, first near the monument, and the second, on the top of the Cross as seen in figure 1. The two eagles are in the same vertical direction. The sky was very clear, so the eagles could see the horizon and observe the Sun set. Each eagle began to fly right at the moment it observed that the Sun disappeared completely.
At the same time, an astronomer is located at the sea-level, at the base of the Bucegi Mountains. Assume that he is in the same vertical direction as the two eagles.
Assuming the atmospheric refraction to be negligible, solve the following questions:

The following information is necessary:
The duration of the sunset measurement starts when the solar disc is tangent to the horizon line and stops when the solar disc completely disappears.
The Earth’s rotational period is TE = 24 h, the radius of the Sun RS = 6.96 * 10^5 km, Earth – Sun distance dES = 14.96 * 10^7 km, the latitude of Heroes Cross is φ = 45º. Radius of Earth RE = 6370 km

B) At a certain moment the next day, 22nd March 2014, the two eagles come back to the Heroes Cross. One of the eagles lands on the top of the vertical pillar of the Cross and the other one land on the horizontal plateau, just at the tip of the shadow of the vertical pillar of the Cross, at that moment of the day when the shadow length is minimum.

C) At midnight, the astronomer visits the cross and, from its top, he identifies a bright star at the limit of the circumpolarity. He named this star “Eagles Star”. Knowing that due to the atmospheric refraction the horizon lowering is ξ = 34', calculate:

parts.question: Calculate the duration of the sunset, measured by the astronomer.
parts.reference: Using the angular diameter of the Sun theta approx 0.00928 rad and formula tau = (theta * TP) / (2 * pi * cos(varphi)), the calculated duration of the sunset is approximately 3 minutes.

parts.question: Calculate the durations of sunsets measured by each of the two eagles and indicate which of the eagles leaves the Cross first. What is the time interval between the moments of the flights of the two eagles?
parts.reference: Calculating horizon-lowering angles and delays due to altitudes H and H+h. The eagle from the plateau leaves first. The time interval between the flights is Delta t approx 3.354 s.

parts.question: B) 1) Calculate the distance between the two eagles and the second eagle’s distance from the cross.
parts.reference: Minimum shadow length occurs at transit. Distance d approx 55.58 m; distance between eagles u_min = h * tan(varphi) = 39.3 m.

parts.question: B) 2) Calculate the length of the horizontal arms of the Cross l_b, if the shadow on the plateau of one of the arm of the cross at this moment has the length u_b = 7 m.
parts.reference: l_b = u_b * tan(varphi) = 7 m * tan(45º) = 7 m.

parts.question: C) 1) The “Eagles star” declination;
parts.reference: Delta_min = 90º - varphi - theta' - Delta alpha_2 approx 42.9º.

parts.question: C) 2) The “Eagles star” maximum height above the horizon.

tasks.title: From Romania …. to Antipod! …with a ballistic messenger
tasks.statement:
The 8th IOAA organizers plan to send to the antipode (the point on the Earth’s surface diametrically opposite to the launch position) the official flag using a ballistic projectile. The projectile will be launched from Romania, and the rotation of the Earth will be neglected.
You may use the value of the gravitational acceleration at Earth surface as g0 = 9.81 m s^-2; the Earth radius R = 6370 km. For part f, use: The Moon albedo alpha_M = 0.12; The Moon radius R_M = 1738 Km; the Earth – Moon distance r_EM = 385000 km; the apparent magnitude of the full moon m_M = -12.7m. You assume that the projectile is perfectly metallic sphere with radius r_projectile = 400 * 10^-3 m and with perfectly reflective surface.

parts.question: a) Calculate the coordinates of the target-point if the launch-point coordinates are: varphi_Romania = 44º North; lambda_Romania = 30º East.
parts.reference: varphi_Antipod = 43º Sud; lambda_Antipod = 150º Vest (or 44º S, 150º W depending on exact coordinates used in formulas; official key gives varphi_Antipod = 43º Sud, lambda_Antipod = 150º Vest).

parts.question: b) Determine the magnitude of the velocity and the launch angle, with respect to the horizon at launch site, in order that the projectile should hit the target.
parts.reference: Launch angle alpha = 30º (elevation beta = 30º), velocity v_0 derived via orbital energy and geometry.

parts.question: c) Calculate the velocity of the projectile when it hits the target.
parts.reference: v_Antipod = v_0 due to conservation of energy.

parts.question: d) Calculate the minimum velocity of the projectile on its trajectory.
parts.reference: Calculated at apogee using vis-viva equation with r_max.

parts.question: e) Calculate the flying –time of the projectile, from the launch to the impact.
parts.reference: Derived using Kepler's third law and area sector equations for the elliptic trajectory.

parts.question: f) Will it be possible that the projectile will be seen by the naked eye when it is at the maximum distance from the Earth.
parts.reference: Apparent magnitude of projectile at apogee is calculated to be about +10.7m, which is greater than the naked eye limit of ~6m, so it cannot be seen.
